title: Chambers incident to a face form its standard parabolic residue
statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] with positive definite symmetric bilinear form $(\ ,\ )$. Let $R\subset E\setminus\{0\}$ be finite and spanning, with $R\cap\mathbf Rr=\{r,-r\}$ for every $r\in R$. Suppose the reflections $s_r(x)=x-2(x,r)(r,r)^{-1}r$ permute $R$ and $2(t,r)(r,r)^{-1}\in\mathbf Z$ for all $r,t\in R$. Let $D\subseteq R$ be a real basis such that every root has integral $D$-coordinates all nonnegative or all nonpositive. Put $H_r=\{x:(x,r)=0\}$, let $W_R\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbf R}(E)$ be generated by all $s_r$, and put $C=\{x:(x,d)>0\text{ for all }d\in D\}$. Chambers mean connected components of $E\setminus\bigcup_{r\in R}H_r$. For $J\subseteq D$ put $W_J=\langle s_j:j\in J\rangle$. If $q\in E$ satisfies $(q,j)=0$ for $j\in J$ and $(q,d)>0$ for $d\in D\setminus J$, then
$$\{B:B\text{ is a chamber and }q\in\overline B\}=\{vC:v\in W_J\}.$$
Moreover $\{r\in R:(q,r)=0\}=R\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf R}(J)$. Thus the roots vanishing at $q$ span a space of dimension $|J|$. The closure is in the usual finite-dimensional topology; $J=\varnothing$, $J=D$, $R=\varnothing$ and $E=0$ are permitted.

proof.text: Write a root as $r=\sum_{d\in D}n_dd$, with the integers $n_d$ all of one sign. Then $(q,r)=\sum_{d\in D\setminus J}n_d(q,d)$ vanishes exactly when every coefficient outside $J$ is zero: all summands have one sign and each $(q,d)$ outside $J$ is strictly positive. Uniqueness of basis coordinates therefore gives $\{r\in R:(q,r)=0\}=R\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf R}(J)$. This root set contains $J$ and is contained in its span, so its span is exactly $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf R}(J)$. The subset $J$ of a basis is a basis of that subspace; [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] gives its dimension $|J|$.

source.place: C.21, printed p.612: same-sign base coordinates; explicit coordinate calculation.

proof.text: Substitution in the formula for $s_r$ gives $s_r^2=1$ and $(s_rx,s_ry)=(x,y)$. Hence every $w\in W_R$ is orthogonal and permutes $R$. Its permutation action on the finite set $R$ is faithful, because $R$ spans $E$; consequently $W_R$ and its subgroup $W_J$ are finite. Each generator $s_j$ of $W_J$ fixes $q$, so every $v\in W_J$ fixes $q$. For the norm $\|x\|=\sqrt{(x,x)}$, it follows that $\|vx-q\|=\|x-q\|$. The formula also gives $wH_r=H_{wr}$, so $W_R$ preserves regular points, meaning the complement of all root hyperplanes.

source.place: C.8, printed p.609, and C.15, p.611: explicit orthogonality and faithful finite permutation action.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-root-chamber-simple-transitivity] with $V=E$ and the given $R,D$: its hypotheses are exactly the root, form and base assumptions here. It says that $C$ is a nonempty chamber and that $vC$ is a chamber for $v\in W_J\subseteq W_R$. Choose $h\in C$. For $t>0$, all simple-root pairings of $q+th$ are positive; hence $q+th\in C$ and $q\in\overline C$ on letting $t\to0$. Since $v$ is an invertible linear map, hence a homeomorphism, $vq=q$ implies $q\in v\overline C=\overline{vC}$. This proves the right-to-left inclusion.

source.place: C.9--C.10, printed pp.609--610, and C.22, p.612; elementary closure limit and equivariance.

proof.text: For the converse let $B$ be a chamber with $q\in\overline B$. Continuity of the finitely many pairings, positive at $q$ for $d\in D\setminus J$, gives $\epsilon>0$ such that $\|x-q\|<\epsilon$ implies $(x,d)>0$ for all such $d$; if this set is empty take any $\epsilon>0$. Choose $y\in B$ in this ball. Among the finite set $W_Jy$ choose $z=vy$ maximizing $(z,h)$, with $h\in C$ as above. If $(z,j)<0$ for some $j\in J$, then $s_jz\in W_Jy$ and $$(s_jz,h)-(z,h)=-2(z,j)(j,h)/(j,j)>0,$$ a contradiction. Thus $(z,j)\geq0$; regularity of $z$ makes each of these pairings strictly positive. Since $v$ fixes $q$ and is orthogonal, $z$ remains in the ball, so its pairings with $D\setminus J$ are positive too. Therefore $z\in C$. The chamber action of [lem-sfb-root-chamber-simple-transitivity] makes $vB$ a chamber; it and $C$ contain $z$, so they are the same connected component. Thus $B=v^{-1}C$ with $v^{-1}\in W_J$, proving the other inclusion. This argument includes $J=\varnothing$ and $J=D$. If $R=\varnothing$, spanning forces $E=0$, the base and $J$ are empty, $q=0$, and the unique chamber is $\{0\}$; both sets in the assertion are singletons and the dimension is zero.
